subject: History
topic: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan — mixed tiers
description: Mysore kingdom, Anglo-Mysore wars, Srirangapatna, rocket warfare, treaty of Mangalore

questions.stem: Haidar Ali was the de-facto ruler of which kingdom in the late 18th century?

options.option_text: The Maratha confederacy with seat at Pune
The Mysore kingdom in southern Karnataka
The Hyderabad state of the Asaf Jahi Nizams
The Travancore state on the Malabar coast

questions.explanation: Haidar Ali (1721-82) — rose from soldier to commander to ruler of Mysore (1761), nominally serving the Wodeyar dynasty as 'Sarvadhikari'. Built up a modern infantry-artillery army with French help. Engaged the British in the First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69, Treaty of Madras restoring status quo). Died during the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1782); succeeded by his son TIPU SULTAN. Distractor 1 = Marathas (Peshwas at Pune). Distractor 3 = Asaf Jahis. Distractor 4 = Travancore was ruled by its own dynasty.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan, often called the 'Tiger of Mysore', died in 1799 defending which fortress against the British?

options.option_text: Bidar fort, in northern Karnataka region
Srirangapatna, on the Cauvery river
Bhondsi fort, in Maharashtra Deccan
Bekal fort, in northern Kerala coast

questions.explanation: Srirangapatna (Seringapatam) — Tipu's island capital, on the Cauvery near Mysore. Fell on 4 May 1799 to British under Lord Wellesley + Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington); Tipu died in the breach. End of FOURTH Anglo-Mysore War (1798-99). Mysore territory split — restored to a child Wodeyar (Krishnaraja Wodeyar III) under British subsidiary alliance, plus annexations to British and to Hyderabad. Tipu's family imprisoned at Vellore Fort — site of 1806 Vellore Mutiny. Distractor 1, 3, 4 are real forts but not associated with Tipu's death.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan was a pioneer in the military use of:

options.option_text: Submarines for naval warfare on the western coast
Iron-cased rockets, technology adopted later by the British
Hot-air balloons used for surveying enemy formations
Steam-powered warships in the Bay of Bengal area

questions.explanation: MYSOREAN ROCKETS — iron-tube-encased gunpowder rockets, range up to ~2 km. Used effectively at Pollilur (1780) by Haidar Ali against East India Company. The British captured many at Srirangapatna (1799); Sir William Congreve studied them at the Royal Arsenal, Woolwich → developed CONGREVE ROCKETS used by British in Napoleonic Wars + War of 1812 (the 'rockets' red glare' line in the US national anthem). Tipu's rockets thus had a direct line to modern artillery rockets. APJ Abdul Kalam (former Indian President + ISRO scientist) cited Mysorean rockets as inspiration.

questions.stem: Which TREATY ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84)?

options.option_text: Treaty of Salbai with the Marathas in 1782
Treaty of Mangalore between Tipu and the British in 1784
Treaty of Seringapatam after the third war in 1792
Treaty of Bassein with the Peshwa Bajirao II in 1802

questions.explanation: Treaty of Mangalore — March 1784. Tipu and the British. Restored prisoners and conquests to status quo ante. Notable as the LAST treaty between an Indian ruler and the British that was negotiated on equal terms (Tipu held the British weaker position then). Distractor 1 — Salbai ended the FIRST Anglo-Maratha War. Distractor 3 — Treaty of Seringapatam ended the THIRD Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92), forcing Tipu to cede half his territory + send two sons as hostages. Distractor 4 — Treaty of Bassein triggered the SECOND Anglo-Maratha War.

questions.stem: How many ANGLO-MYSORE WARS were fought between the British East India Company and the Mysore kingdom?

options.option_text: Two wars, in 1767-69 and in 1798-99
Four wars, between 1767 and 1799
Six wars, similar to the Anglo-Maratha sequence
Three wars, all of which Tipu Sultan led

questions.explanation: Four Anglo-Mysore Wars: 1ST (1767-69) — Treaty of Madras (Haidar against EIC + Hyderabad + Marathas). 2ND (1780-84) — Treaty of Mangalore (Haidar early, Tipu finished). 3RD (1790-92) — Treaty of Seringapatam (Tipu lost half territory, two sons as hostages). 4TH (1798-99) — Tipu killed at Srirangapatna; Mysore largely annexed/restored to Wodeyars under subsidiary alliance. Distractor 1 misses 2 of the 4. Distractor 3 = Anglo-Maratha sequence (3 wars in fact, not 6). Distractor 4 — Tipu led only 2nd (partly), 3rd, 4th (his father led the 1st).

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan's foreign policy was distinctive in seeking diplomatic ties with which European power against the British?

options.option_text: Portugal, then losing influence in Asian trade routes
Revolutionary / Napoleonic France, particularly after 1789
Russia, the rising European empire from the north
Spain, with bases in the Philippines and far-east Asia

questions.explanation: Tipu corresponded with Revolutionary France: planted a 'Liberty Tree' at Srirangapatna (1797), styled himself 'Citoyen Tipu' (Citizen Tipu) in Jacobin fashion, sought Napoleonic alliance after Bonaparte's Egyptian expedition (1798). The Treaty of Hyderabad (1798) — British forced Hyderabad's Nizam to dismiss French officers, isolating Tipu. The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War followed, leading to Tipu's death. Distractor 1 — Portugal had no significant influence by then. Distractor 3 — Russian engagement in S Asia came later. Distractor 4 — Spain was waning.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan introduced an administrative + revenue innovation that significantly increased state revenue. He:

options.option_text: Sold all the state's land directly to private buyers
Eliminated middlemen zamindars and collected revenue directly
Reduced agricultural taxes to one-tenth of normal levels
Banned all foreign trade through coastal Mysore ports

questions.explanation: Tipu abolished the intermediary zamindari/poligar system in much of Mysore — assessed and collected land revenue DIRECTLY by state officials (similar to Sher Shah Suri's earlier reforms). Increased state revenue, undermined the local landed aristocracy. Also encouraged commerce: established trading depots at foreign ports (Muscat, Pegu, Aden, China), built a state navy, established sericulture (silk industry — ~21 silk production centres), introduced new tax systems. Distractor 1 — false. Distractor 3 — taxes were not slashed dramatically. Distractor 4 — opposite of true; he encouraged trade.
